summary: William Dwight Whitney worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Williams College, Yale under Salisbury, Berlin under Weber and Lepsius, and Tübingen under Roth. He served as professor of Sanskrit and comparative philology at Yale (1853, 1869–1894).

William Edelglass works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He has served as a teacher at Colby College (attested 2007), a professor at Marlboro College (attested 2013), and a visiting professor at the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics.

William Edward Soothill was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of London. He served as director at Shanxi University (1907–1911), at National Central University (1911), and as professor of Chinese at Oxford (1920–1935).

William Erskine was an Indology, Iranian and Central Asian, and history scholar who studied at the Royal High School and the University of Edinburgh. He co-founded the Asiatic Society of Mumbai and served the Literary Society of Bombay (c. 1804–1823).
William Evans Hoyle studied at Owens College from around 1871 to 1874 and subsequently at Christ Church, Oxford, from around 1874 to 1877.

William F. Powell is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He has been affiliated with the University of California, Santa Barbara, where he was attested in 1986 and as emeritus and research professor in 2026.

William Fairfield Warren worked in religious studies and philosophy. Educated at Wesleyan, Mystical Seven, and Andover Theological Seminary, he taught at the Methodist Episcopal Missionary Institute (1860–1866) and served as Boston University's first president and professor (1873–1911).

William Foster studied at the University of London before working in history and Indology. He held posts at the India Office from 1882 to 1927, including registrar and superintendent of records, and later served as Hakluyt Society president (1928–1945).

William Foxwell Albright was an archaeologist, linguist, and religious studies scholar educated at Upper Iowa University and Johns Hopkins. He was acting director at the American Schools of Oriental Research (1921–1922) and Spence Professor at Johns Hopkins (1929–1958).
William Francklin was an Indology and history scholar who was educated at Westminster School and studied at Trinity College, Cambridge, from around 1781 to 1782.

William Frederic Sinclair was an Indology and history scholar who studied at the Royal School, Armagh. He joined the Indian Civil Service in 1866 and served in administrative posts in the Bombay Presidency from around 1871 to 1897.
William Frederick Travers O'Connor was a Tibetology scholar who studied at Charterhouse School and the Royal Military Academy, Woolwich. He joined the Royal Artillery in 1890.
William Frederick Webster studied Indology at the City of London School, Lincoln's Inn, and Trinity College, Cambridge, where he studied under Edward Byles Cowell in 1874.

William G. Archer was an Indology and history scholar who studied at Cambridge and SOAS University of London. From 1949 to 1959, he served as Keeper of the Indian Section at the Victoria and Albert Museum.
William George Grey was a linguist and Indologist who received an honorary degree from the University of Cambridge. He served as Lecturer in Urdu at Gonville and Caius College from 1929 to 1940.

William H. Nienhauser, Jr. is a Sinologist educated at Indiana University under Irving Yucheng Lo and Friedrich Bischoff, and at Bonn. He served as professor and Halls-Bascom Professor of Classical Chinese Literature at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from 1983.

William H. Wiser, an Indologist, studied at the University of Chicago and Cornell University. He worked at Sam Higginbottom University in 1915 and served as Professor of Rural Sociology at North India Theological College from 1933 to 1941.

William Harlen Gilbert, Jr. worked in Indology and sociology after earning his PhD from the University of Chicago in 1935. He taught sociology at Auburn University (1936–1937) and served at the Library of Congress from around 1941 to 1968.
William Harrison Moreland, an Indology and history scholar, studied at Clifton College and Trinity College, Cambridge. He served in the Indian Civil Service from around 1889 to 1914.
William Hay Macnaghten was an Indology scholar who was educated at Charterhouse School and later studied at Fort William College in 1816.
